source_text: Καὶ κατανοοῦντι, τί ἀπιστότερον ἂν μᾶλλον δόξαι, ἢ εἰ ἐν σώματι μὴ ὑπήρχομεν καί τις ἔλεγεν, ἐκ μικρᾶς τινος ῥανίδος τῆς τοῦ ἀνθρωπείου σπέρματος δυνατὸν ὀστέα τε καὶ νεῦρα καὶ σάρκας εἰκονοποιηθέντα, οἷα ὁρῶμεν, γενέσθαι; Ἔστω γὰρ νῦν ἐφ᾿ ὑποθέσεως λεγόμενον.· εἴ τις ἱ μῖν μὴ οὖσι τοιούτοις μηδὲ τοιούτων ἔλεγε, τὸ σπέρμα τὸ ἀνθρώπειον δεικνὺς καὶ εἰκόνα γραπτήν, ἐκ τοῦ τοιοῦδε τοιόνδε γενέσθαι διαβεβαιούμενος, πρὶν ἰδεῖν γενόμενον ἐπιστεύσατε; οὐκ ἄν τις τολμήσειεν ἀντειπεῖν. Τὸν αὐτὸν οὗν τρόπον διὰ τὸ μήπω ἑωρακέναι ὑμᾶς ἀναστάντα νεκρὸν ἀπιστία ἔχει. Ἀλλ᾿ ὃν τρόπον τὴν ἀρχὴν οὐκ ἂν ἐπιστεύσατε ἐκ τῆς μικρᾶς ῥανίδος δυνατὸν τοιούτους γενέσθαι, καὶ ὁρᾶτε γινομένους, τὸν αὐτὸν τρόπον λογίσασθε, ὅτι διαλυθέντα καὶ δίκην σπερμάτων εἰς γῆν διαχυθέντα τὰ ἀνθρώπεια σώματα κατὰ καιρὸν προστάξει θεοῦ ἀναστῆναι καὶ „ἀφθαρσίαν ἐνδύσασθαι“ οὐκ ἀδύνατον. Ποίαν γὰρ ἀξίαν θεοῦ δύναμιν λέγουσιν οἱ φάσκοντες εἰς ἐκεῖνο χωρεῖν ἕκαστον ἐξ οὗπερ ἐγένετο, καὶ παρὰ ταῦτα μηδὲν ἄλλο δύνασθαι μηδὲ τὸν θεόν, οὐκ ἔχομεν λέγειν· ἀλλ᾿ ἐκεῖνο συνορῶμεν, ὅτι οὐκ ἂν ἐπίστευσαν δυνατὸν εἶναι τοιούτους ποτὲ γενέσθαι, ὁποίους καὶ ἑαυτοὺς καὶ τὸν σύμπαντα κόσμον καὶ ἐξ ὁποίων γεγενημένα ὁρῶσι. Κρεῖττον δὲ πιστεύειν καὶ τὰ τῇ ἑαυτῶν φύσει καὶ ἀνθρώποις ἀδύνατα, ἢ ὁμοίως τοῖς ἄλλοις ἀπιστεῖν παρειλήφαμεν, ἐπειδὴ καὶ τὸν ἡμέτερον διδάσκαλον Ἰησοῦν Χριστὸν ἔγνωμεν εἰπόντα· „Τὰ ἀδύνατα παρὰ ἀνθρώποις δυνατὰ παρὰ θεῷ“. Καὶ εἶπε· „Μὴ φοβεῖσθε τοὺς ἀναιροῦντας ὑμᾶς καὶ μετὰ ταῦτα μὴ δυναμένους τι ποιῆσαι, φοβήθητε δὲ τὸν μετὰ τὸ ἀποθανεῖν δυνάμενον καὶ ψυχὴν καὶ σῶμα εἰς γέενναν ἐμβαλεῖν“. Ἡ δὲ γέεννά ἐστι τόπος, ἔνθα κολάζεσθαι μέλλουσιν οἱ ἀδίκως βιώσαντες καὶ μὴ πιστεύοντες ταῦτα γενήσεσθαι, ὅσα ὁ θεὸς διὰ τοῦ Χριστοῦ ἐδίδαξε.
pass_a_gloss: And to one considering, what would be more unbelievable, if someone were saying, while we are not in body, that from a small drop of human seed it is possible for bones and sinews and flesh to be formed in the image, such as we see, to come into being? Let it be said now on the basis of a hypothesis. For if someone were showing you the human seed and a drawn image, guaranteeing that from such a thing such a thing comes into being, would you have believed before seeing it come into being? No one would have dared to speak against. In the same way, therefore, because you have not yet seen a risen dead person, there is unbelief. But just as you would not have believed at the beginning that from a small drop it is possible for such people to come into being, and you see them coming into being, in the same way consider that it is not impossible for human bodies, having been dissolved and scattered into the earth like seeds, to rise again at the command of God and to put on incorruption. For what kind of worth of God's power do those who say that each thing goes back to what it came from, and besides this is able to do nothing else, nor God, we do not have to say; but we observe that thing, that they would not have believed it possible for such people to come into being at any time, such as they see themselves and the whole world and from which they have come into being. But it is better to believe both the things that are beyond their own nature and impossible for humans, than to disbelieve in the same way as the others, since we have known our teacher Jesus Christ to have said: 'The things that are impossible with humans are possible with God.' And he said: 'Do not fear those who kill you and after that are not able to do anything, but fear the one who after death is able to throw both soul and body into Gehenna.' And Gehenna is a place where those who have lived unrighteously and do not believe these things to come into being, which God taught through Christ, are about to be punished.

bible_refs.note: The things that are impossible with humans are possible with God
Do not fear those who kill you and after that are not able to do anything

pass_b_english: Consider this: what could seem more incredible than the claim that, while we did not yet exist in bodily form, a tiny drop of human seed could produce bones, sinews, and flesh shaped exactly as we see them? Suppose someone showed you that seed and a drawing of the fully formed body, insisting that the one comes from the other. Would you have believed it before actually watching it happen? No one would dare deny it. Yet you refuse to believe in the resurrection simply because you have not yet seen a dead person rise. But just as you would not have believed at the start that such bodies could arise from a mere drop, even though you now watch it happen every day, so you should reason that it is not impossible for human bodies, once dissolved and scattered into the earth like seed, to rise again at God's command and put on incorruption. What kind of divine power do those people attribute to God who say that each thing can only return to the elements it came from, and that nothing else is possible — not even for God? We need not answer that; we simply observe that they would never have believed such beings could ever come to be — beings like themselves, like the whole world, and like the very elements from which they originated. It is better to trust that the things impossible by human nature and power are possible for God, than to persist in unbelief like the rest. For we have known our teacher Jesus Christ, who said, "The things that are impossible with humans are possible with God" (Luke 18:27). And he said, "Do not fear those who kill you and after that can do nothing more, but fear the one who after death is able to throw both soul and body into Gehenna" (Matthew 10:28). Gehenna is the place where those who have lived unrighteously and refuse to believe that these things will come to pass, which God taught through Christ, are destined to be punished.

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the hypothetical nature of the seed argument and the distinction between human impossibility and divine possibility. Scripture citations in Pass B (Luke 18:27 and Matthew 10:28) correctly identify the source of the quoted material in the Greek.
